title: CliffCompaction: Cost-Efficient Compaction for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
why_read: A practical technique for reducing the cost of long-running coding AI agents by compacting context without rewriting or degrading it, backed by concrete benchmark gains including matching a larger model at lower cost.
analysis: Long-running AI coding agents accumulate huge amounts of context over multi-million-token sessions, and this paper's CliffCompaction method reduces that cost by up to 50% by only truncating or dropping old content rather than summarizing or rewriting it, which the authors argue prevents information drift over many compaction passes. They report solid gains on Terminal-Bench and state-of-the-art results on KernelBench, including letting a mid-tier model match a more expensive one at lower cost. The open-sourced, scaffold-agnostic implementation compatible with Claude Code and Codex increases its practical value for engineers building agentic coding tools. This is a concrete, actionable systems contribution rather than a purely theoretical exercise.
